questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
The driver will have trouble seeing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Usually, this means the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position makes them more likely to see you.

questions.question: You must be at least this age to get an intermediate permit:
questions.correctAnswerText: 16 years old
questions.explanation: In Wyoming, you can get an instruction permit for a motorcycle at age 15. At age 16, if you have completed enough practice riding hours, you can get an intermediate permit.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to drive around a train.

questions.question: Helmets are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards every time they ride. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries if you crash.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is easiest to see when riding in which lane position?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best when following a car because the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or road conditions change.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to stay in control during a turn?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up through the turn.
questions.explanation: To stay in control while turning, slow down before you enter the turn. Look ahead in the direction you want to go, lean your motorcycle the right way, and gently use the throttle to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: Motorcycles need:

options.text: Less stopping distance than larger vehicles.
The same stopping distance as larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same stopping distance as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep enough space between you and other vehicles. Motorcycles need as much room to stop as other vehicles do.

questions.question: When entering a curve, position your motorcycle:

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle the road and traffic.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that is safe for the current conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: If you are towing a trailer on a motorcycle, your following distance should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Stay closer to the vehicle ahead so you can see by its lights.
Keep your normal speed to avoid being hit from behind.
Slow down and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Visibility is lower at night, and you need more time and space to react to hazards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the road ahead.
Stop completely. Proceed only when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Proceed only when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, check for other traffic or pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When riding on packed snow, how much should you reduce your speed?
questions.correctAnswerText: Half of your normal speed.
questions.explanation: On packed snow, reduce your speed by at least half. Take extra care on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Which statement is true about motorcycle brakes?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's stopping power.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic will merge.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that traffic will merge ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the road edge mean?

options.text: It marks the right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It marks the right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the road edge marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves on metal bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Shift down to a lower gear right away.
Zigzag across the bridge until you reach the other side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed and steer straight.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves on metal gratings or rain grooves, simply relax and go straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than the natural weaving.

questions.question: How should you carry a load on your motorcycle?

options.text: On the gas tank in front of you.
Piled high against the back of the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over the rear axle.
questions.explanation: Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on a motorcycle.

questions.question: When reacting to a road hazard, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your horn or lights to alert others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid communicating with other drivers.
questions.explanation: To handle hazards safely, communicate with other drivers using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed as needed and change your lane position if necessary.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can control your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from a hazard, apply light pressure to the handgrip on the side of your intended escape route.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: It gives you more time to react to dangers.
It stops you from finding an escape route.
It gives you room to move your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops you from finding an escape route.
questions.explanation: Keep space between you and the vehicle ahead. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Space also lets you safely move your motorcycle when needed.

questions.question: Unless a different speed limit is posted, what is the maximum speed on the interstate?
questions.correctAnswerText: 80 mph
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit on interstate highways in Wyoming is 75 or 80 mph. If you see a different speed limit posted, follow that sign instead.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes.
It is okay for a motorcyclist to weave between lanes.
A motorcyclist should ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes.
questions.explanation: Riding between stopped or slow-moving vehicles is dangerous. Other vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to stay safe, even though they are small.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of a small vehicle like a motorcycle. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately see your speed and location.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
You should go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, if you arrive at the same time as another vehicle, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
